**Klynge NORD** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) in Denmark that operates within [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] [^src5]. It is one of the regional organizational units monitored by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) to evaluate and improve the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] (AF) [^src1]. 

The cluster is significant for its performance on national clinical quality indicators. Notably, Klynge NORD is recognized as one of the healthcare clusters that successfully meets the national standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation therapy]] in newly diagnosed AF patients [^src1]. In the reported data, the cluster achieved a result of 92.2% for this indicator [^src1]. 

Beyond initial treatment, Klynge NORD's clinical outcomes and adherence to guidelines are tracked across multiple metrics and timeframes. For example, during the period from July 1, 2018, to June 30, 2019, the proportion of AF patients receiving anticoagulation therapy in the cluster was 94.1% (95% CI: 90.3–96.7) [^src3]. The cluster's data is also integral to broader geographical and comparative analyses, such as national mapping of stroke (apopleksi) incidence across healthcare clusters, where Klynge NORD is plotted alongside other units like [[klynge-syd|Klynge SYD]] and [[sundhedsklynge-nord|Sundhedsklynge Nord]] [^src4]. 

Furthermore, Klynge NORD is evaluated on a wide array of supplementary quality indicators. These include 1-year and 2-year treatment coverage rates [^src2], annual P-creatinine monitoring for patients on DOACs [^src4], and the incidence of severe bleeding and heart failure within one year of a new diagnosis [^src6]. Additionally, the cluster's specific outcomes regarding heart failure development and mortality are extensively detailed in the 2024 report [^src7]. In subsequent reporting periods, such as the 2025 annual report, Klynge NORD continues to be assessed on metrics including structured patient education [^src8], severe bleeding among prevalent patients [^src9], and waiting times for anticoagulation therapy [^src10], [^src11].
